title: A 97.4%-Peak-Efficiency Always-Half-Inductor-Current Hybrid Bidirectional Converter With Adaptive Target Current Tracking for USB-to-2-Cell Bidirectional Power Transfer
problem: Bidirectional DC-DC converters for 2-cell batteries (6-8.4V) suffer from high inductor DC resistance losses and require expensive high-voltage transistors, limiting efficiency in both forward (USB charging) and on-the-go (OTG power delivery) modes.
motivation: Portable devices increasingly require bidirectional power transfer between USB and 2-cell batteries with high efficiency while minimizing size and cost constraints.
method: The design uses an always-half-inductor-current hybrid converter topology that reduces peak inductor current by half compared to conventional boost/buck topologies, thereby minimizing DCR losses. Adaptive target current tracking dynamically optimizes operating point across loading conditions. The hybrid approach operates as a boost in forward mode and buck in OTG mode with reduced inductor stress.
key_novelty: Always-half-inductor-current hybrid topology with adaptive target current tracking achieving peak efficiency while reducing inductor and transistor stress.
contributions: Hybrid converter topology reducing inductor current by 50% vs. conventional topologies
Adaptive target current tracking for dynamic optimization
Reduced HV transistor requirements through optimized voltage distribution
primary_theme: High-efficiency hybrid bidirectional converter for portable device battery management
